_comment: Rules of the home conventions (hooks/RULES.md): what hooks/tools/conformance.py scans, the vocabularies it checks against, and the event lists of the shared helpers (hooks/lib/hookio.py); their numbers and the generated hook command are values in config/home.json section hooks. A registry (config/registry/): config/local.json can't override it. Paths are relative to the home root.
_note_scan_dirs: Top-level directories the conformance checker walks; the files under skip_parts are left out.
_note_state_path_owner: S2: the only files that may spell the state directory's name.
_note_state_writers: S7: the only files that may write JSON or JSON lines (atomic write, single-write append).
_note_tools: Command-line tools that write tracked files (settings, snapshots, generated code), not runtime state: S5 and S7 don't apply, and H3 (hook docstring) doesn't either.
_note_header_parsers: R4: the only files that may match report header lines with a regex or startswith.
_note_time_source: X1/X2: the only files that may read the wall clock into a stored timestamp.
_note_header_keys: R4: report header keys whose parsing is reserved to header_parsers.
_note_unit_suffixes: C3: a numeric settings value's key ends in one of these, or a key above it does (a value-as-key table such as budget.fallback_minutes, agent name -> minutes), or it is listed in unitless_keys.
_note_unitless_keys: C3: numeric keys that have no unit: schema (a format version), estimate_fixed_quantile (a quantile, 0 to 1).
_note_forbidden_rules: Rules of hooks/tools/conformance.py whose debt reached zero: a violation of one fails conformance.py and tests/test_conformance.py even with --write-snapshot --allow-new, and the snapshot may not list one. A rule joins once its snapshot entries are gone; it never leaves.
_note_test_forbidden_paths: T3: spellings of the real home tree a test may not use in code (a test loads the tree under test).
_note_naming_exempt_prefixes: H2: function names that must keep another spelling (pytest hooks and tests, ast visitors).
_note_guard_events: hookio: events whose guard failure can be refused through the JSON output; other events exit 2.
_note_block_once_events: hookio: guard events where a refusal keeps the agent working, so a crashing guard blocks at most once per distinct error per agent or session, then lets the stop through with a warning.
_note_hook_ceilings_seconds: The outer timeout of each gate's settings.json registration (a safety net, hand-kept in settings.json, checked by hooks/tools/hook-entries.py --check-settings: installed >= these), keyed by the gate's deadline in home.json quality.hook_timeouts; a registration takes the largest of its keys. The gate enforces its deadline itself (qg_common.startDeadline), and a deadline above its ceiling is invalid in home.json (an error) and in local.json (home's value is used). 1.5 x the home deadlines (1800 s; 3600 s for the handback and stop entries): room for the gate to report after its deadline and for a local deadline above home's.
_note_builtin_agent_types: hook-entry.py: agent_type values Claude Code itself has (no agents/<name>.md); any other name without an agents/<name>.md in this home or the project warns the person once and records a hook-failed event. Add a name when Claude Code adds an agent type.
